record.original_question: If X is a first-countable LOTS and X squared minus the diagonal is hereditarily paracompact, must X have a point-countable base? Also, can a Souslin space have the property that its square minus the diagonal is hereditarily paracompact?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Suppose X is a LOTS that is first-countable and hereditarily paracompact off of the diagonal (i.e., X2 \ ∆ is hereditarily paracompact). Must X have a point-countable base? Is it possible that a Souslin space can be hereditarily paracompact off of the diagonal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a set X equipped with a linear order < and the topology generated by the open intervals. A topological space is hereditarily paracompact if every subspace is paracompact. A base B for a topology is point-countable if every point belongs to at most countably many members of B. A Souslin space is a nonseparable LOTS with countable cellularity (i.e., every collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty open sets is countable). Let Δ = {(x,x) : x ∈ X} ⊆ X² denote the diagonal.

(a) Suppose X is a first-countable LOTS such that X² \ Δ is hereditarily paracompact. Must X have a point-countable base?

(b) Is it consistent (or provable in ZFC) that there exists a Souslin space X such that X² \ Δ is hereditarily paracompact?
artifact.status_search_result: A survey by Bennett and Lutzer on ordered spaces notes that if a Souslin line exists, then there exists a Souslin space X with X² \ Δ hereditarily paracompact, giving a consistent positive answer to part (b). The first-countable LOTS question (a) about whether the property forces a point-countable base does not appear to have been resolved in ZFC in available sources, so the overall problem is at best partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Recent Developments in the Topology of Ordered Spaces (Bennett–Lutzer)
status_evidence.snippet: If there is a Souslin space, then there is a Souslin space X such that X² \ Δ is hereditarily paracompact.
status_evidence.claim: Part (b) has a consistent positive answer assuming the existence of a Souslin line.

status_evidence.title: Problems from Topology Proceedings
status_evidence.snippet: Questions concerning LOTS that are hereditarily paracompact off the diagonal and point-countable bases.
status_evidence.claim: The first-countable LOTS question remains a stated open problem in topology problem lists.
